title: 'Coyote vs. Acme' Cast and Crew Held a 'Funeral Screening' After the Movie Was Shelved: 'Was Emotional in So Many Ways'
text:
The 'Coyote vs. Acme' team held a 'funeral screening' when they thought the movie would never be released.
‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Cast and Crew Held a ‘Funeral Screening’ After the Movie Was Shelved: ‘Was Emotional in So Many Ways’ What do you do when you think your movie will never see the light of day?
Have a “funeral screening,” of course.from the studio in March 2025 and slated it for theatrical release. Audiences will finally get to see the “Looney Tunes” movie on Aug. 28.
'Ketticè' Review: An Amusing, Original Portrait of Adolescent Ennui Against a Backdrop of Adult CluelessnessVariety at the film’s L.A. premiere on Wednesday, “It’s so horrible. It’s like, really easy to blame yourself. You almost feel like, ‘Was I the problem? ’ You’re devastated for the hundreds of people who have worked on this far longer than I have.
It feels like a funeral. ”Director Dave Green said there were “many, many times” he thought “Coyote vs. Acme” would never come out. Despite his disappointment, he described the mood at the “funeral screening” as “celebratory. ” “You can have a New Orleans funeral, a jazz band walking up the street, just having a celebration,” Green joked.
“That screening for us was emotional in so many ways. It was a bit of a party because we were able to share the movie with friends and other filmmakers who had never seen the movie. And I got to share it with Will and Lana, who never got to see the final movie. So that moment was so charged and electric, and the room played so hot.
” “Coyote vs. Acme” sees “Looney Tunes” villain Wile E. Coyote take the Acme Corporation to court after being injured countless times from using its gadgets .
